name: redact-entities
summary: Redact person, organization, and location mentions from free text using text.detect-entities' real DistilBERT-NER forward pass.
description: Runs the exact same tokenize -> DistilBERT-NER forward pass -> BIO-decode pipeline as text.detect-entities (registry#465, dslim/distilbert-NER, Apache-2.0), reused directly via a source-level dependency rather than duplicated, then substitutes a bracketed placeholder ("[PER]", "[ORG]", "[LOC]", "[MISC]") for each detected entity span instead of returning raw entity data -- copying everything else through unchanged. A real model forward pass at execution time, not a keyword list or regex-based masking. Second pick (after audio.transcribe-speech@1.1.0's VAD gate, registry#477) from a post-#473 downstream-capability review of this session's shipped model engines: no new model, no new license/verification burden -- same weight table, same license record as text.detect-entities. A new capability id, not a version of text.detect-entities, since "redact" is a genuinely different action from "detect" for a caller (different intent, different output shape), not a refinement of the same one. 1.1.1 inherits text.detect-entities@1.1.1's word-level aggregation fix (registry#611): a multi-piece entity such as 'Acme Corp' is now replaced by one '[ORG]' instead of '[ORG][ORG][ORG]'. Does not detect speech, translate, resolve entities against a knowledge base, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.

use_cases.scenario: As a privacy export reviewer, I want person, organization, and location mentions blanked out of a document before it leaves a privacy boundary, so that a forwarded support ticket or shared transcript doesn't carry PII a vendor or auditor shouldn't see.

input_example.text: Sarah Chen from Acme Corp will follow up with the Berlin team next week.

output_example.redacted_text: [PER] from [ORG] will follow up with the [LOC] team next week.

use_cases.scenario: As a privacy export reviewer, I want each multi-piece name (a person like 'Elon Musk', an organization like 'SpaceX') replaced by exactly one placeholder, so that no fragment of a detected entity leaks through and the redacted text stays readable.

input_example.text: Elon Musk founded SpaceX in California.

use_cases.scenario: As a privacy export reviewer, I want text with no detected entities returned completely unchanged, so that redaction never alters content that doesn't need it.

input_example.text: The quarterly report is due next Friday.

output_example.redacted_text: The quarterly report is due next Friday.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies a text string (may be empty).

postconditions.description: Every byte of the input not covered by a detected entity span appears unchanged, in order, in redacted_text; each detected span is replaced by exactly one bracketed placeholder ([PER]/[ORG]/[LOC]/[MISC]).
Identical input yields identical output within one WASM instantiation. Cross-instantiation / cross-host-architecture byte-identity is NOT proven -- see risk.determinism_class.

side_effects.description: Produces a redacted string in memory; does not log, persist, or transmit input text.

provenance.author: enricopiovesan
provenance.spec_ref: registry#481, second pick from the post-#473 'Five Engines, What Next' downstream-capability review, after audio.transcribe-speech@1.1.0's VAD gate (#477). Reuses text.detect-entities' (#465) DistilBERT-NER engine directly via a source-level path dependency on that crate's new lib.rs (split out of its single main.rs the same way audio-detect-speech-segments was split for #477) -- no new model, no new verification burden.

authoring.test_evidence: registry#611 fix: decode_entities now aggregates WordPiece tokens into whole words (first sub-token's label, full-word span) before BIO merging. text-detect-entities: 24 #[test] cases (5 new: B-on-continuation merge, first-piece-only labeling, O-first-piece suppression, adjacent-B words stay separate, per-word index assignment); cargo llvm-cov functions=100%, lines=97.52%, regions=96.75%. text-redact-entities: 10 tests, 100% functions/lines/regions. Verified on the real model (wasm32 --features full-model under wasmtime): every use_case output_example regenerated from the built artifact; extra sentences with accented/hyphenated names (Élysée Palace, São Paulo, Okonjo-Iweala) return whole entities with byte offsets matching input.text[start..end].
